taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes P. ainsworthi was tentatively removed from synonymy of P. mississippi by Pierson et al. (2020); the species was formerly part of P. glutinosus.
fieldMarks: Medium to large terrestrial salamander, about 4-6.5 in.
Black to bluish-black with numerous white, yellow or brassy spots on back, tail and sides; heavy white lateral flecking in some; white spotting on chin and throat; plain belly.
Cannot be told from other members of the slimy salamander complex by appearance alone.
behavior: Forages on the surface at night or in rain but typically stays near its burrow; adults defend small territories.
Terrestrial breeder with no aquatic larval stage; females guard 1-33 eggs from a cavity roof through 2-3 months of development.
Sticky tail secretion deters predators; goes underground in dry or freezing weather.
habitat: Forested areas: maritime and river-bottom hardwoods and pine forests; under rotting logs, branches, rocks, leaf litter, in rock crevices, caves and rubbish piles.
range: Southwestern Kentucky, western Tennessee, western Alabama, most of Mississippi and a small part of southeastern Louisiana, west of the Tennessee River on the Coastal Plain. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Other slimy salamanders (Plethodon glutinosus complex)
lookalikes.howToTell: Identification based on appearance is impossible; range and genetics separate them.
